title: Building Faster Fund plan and dog designation appeal
subtitle: Heritage designations for two properties, remediation, stormwater work, land for future housing, and a prohibited dog designation.
overview: Council met electronically in a special meeting because the Council Chamber technology is being renovated. The main business was a Building Faster Fund Investment Plan that would allocate $14M to three City projects: $1M for Bramm Yards remediation, $3M for stormwater improvements at Sandrock Creek and Meadowlane Park, and $10M for land acquisition for future housing. The Chief Financial Officer was delegated authority to submit the plan {{vote:m2}}. Because two councillors declared conflicts of interest, each project was voted on separately, and each was carried.

Council also dealt with a dangerous dog designation appeal. It ratified the appeal committee's decision to designate a dog as prohibited rather than dangerous {{vote:m3}}. The appeal had been filed by the Humane Society of Kitchener-Waterloo and Stratford Perth.

Council also gave third reading to by-laws designating 10 Duke Street West and 60 Victoria Street North as properties of cultural heritage value. It then met in closed session on a potential land acquisition matter. The minutes report no outcome from that session.

decisions.detail: The Chief Financial Officer was delegated authority to submit a $14M Investment Plan covering Bramm Yards remediation, Sandrock Creek–Meadowlane Park stormwater work and land acquisition for future housing.
Council ratified the Dog Designation Appeal Committee's decision to designate the dog as prohibited, as amended from the original dangerous designation.
Council gave third reading to by-laws designating 10 Duke Street West and 60 Victoria Street North as having historic and cultural heritage value or interest.
